newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices continue to strengthen.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices continue to strengthen.

text.p: Australian wool prices rose sharply this week, increasing on average by three percent at sales in Sydney, Melbourne and Melbourne, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said on Friday.
The eastern market indicator rose 19 cents to 659 cents a kg clean while the western indicator remained at 602 cents with no sales in Fremantle.
A total of 52,623 bales were offered with a pass-in rate of 5.4 percent, the council said.
The wool international stockpile totalled 1,733,158. Trade competition was led by Japanese and Chinese buyers with support from Western European buyers and local mills.

The Council said while this upward movement in prices is very welcome, albeit long overdue, news for growers, there are increasing reports of firms at the fabric and garment making stages strongly resisting any increase in prices of their raw material inputs.
"This makes it very difficult for topmakers and spinners to operate at profitable margins, which ultimately must have an adverse effect on greasy wool prices.
However, the likely timing of such a development remains as difficult as ever to judge," the council said.
In the futures market, a total of 261 lots were traded in the 21 micron contract for the week ending April 23. Open interest increased by 21 contracts to 783.
The June 1997 contract rose 32 cents to 783 cents/kg clean.
Sales next week are in Sydney and Fremantle with 58,800 bales rostered for sale.
